After RiboPilot annotates a contig (see
[Get started](RiboPilot.html#samples-contigs-and-records)), it runs a
set of automatic quality checks and
raises a **curation warning** for anything that looks unusual. Warnings do not change your 
assemblies or annotations, they simply flag something that may need your
attention.

You can find warnings in three places:

- the **Checks** column of the Assemble and Annotation Review tables, which sums up
  every check in a few words
- the **Warnings** column of Annotation Review, which counts the warnings on the
  contig as a whole
- the **Curation warnings** panel of a contig's window, which lists the contig's
  warnings and, below them, each feature that has a warning

# What the warnings mean

| Warning | Source | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|---|
| `missing_18S`, `missing_5.8S`, `missing_28S` | contig | One of the three rRNA genes was not found. | Expected when the contig contains only part of the nuclear rDNA complex. Otherwise look at **Coverage and windowed BLAST** for a break. |
| `missing_ITS1`, `missing_ITS2` | contig | A spacer was not found between its two genes. | Usually follows a missing gene. If both genes are there, check the boundaries in **Edit active feature boundaries**. |
| `out_of_order` | contig | The features are not in the order 18S, ITS1, 5.8S, ITS2, 28S. | Possible assembly error. Export marks it `misassembly`. Check the feature map and read coverage before you submit it. |
| `overlap` | contig and feature | A feature overlaps the one before it. | Move the boundary in **Edit active feature boundaries**. The export marks it `misassembly`. |
| `gap` | contig and feature | An annotation gap between two features. Gaps of 5 bases or fewer are closed when the contig is annotated, so a new contig only gets `gap` for a larger one. | Check the boundaries, and extend the gene or spacer if the gap is part of it. |
| `wrong_strand` | contig and feature | A feature lies on the opposite strand from the rest. | Likely a misassembly or a wrong call. Check the feature model. |
| `length` | feature | The feature is shorter or longer than expected (tables below). | Common for the spacers, and often fine. Check that the boundaries look right. |
| `truncated` | feature | Less than 90 percent of the gene's rRNA model was recovered. | Nothing: the export writes the gene as partial. |
| `low_identity` | feature | The gene falls below a minimum sequence similarity threshold (tables below), and the reference covers at least half of the gene. | An assembly error, or a group with few other rRNA references. Look at the **Reference alignment**. |
| `contaminant` | contig | The contig BLAST best hit is from a different phylum than your sample. | Check the contig before you lock it: it may be another organism's rDNA. Lock and the Export window ask about it until you mark it Reviewed. |
| `contaminant_unchecked` | contig | The contamination check could not run: the BLAST screen has no usable hit for the contig, or your sample's lineage is unknown. | If NCBI could not be reached, run the sample again once it can (see [Troubleshooting](Troubleshooting.html)). If the sample has no taxon, set one in the Taxonomy step. |
| `not_nuclear_rdna` | contig | The BLAST screen's best hit is not a nuclear rDNA record, for example a mitochondrial or bacterial rRNA. | The contig may not be nuclear rDNA. Check its features and hits before you keep it. |
| `no_clade_ruleset` | contig | Your sample's group has no ruleset of its own, so the generic animal ranges were used. | Nothing. See [How the checks are tuned per group](#how-the-checks-are-tuned-per-group). |

Two more columns have results from additional checks. **ITSx Warnings** reports what standard ITSx
check finds for the contig (see [the ITSx check](GenBank-Submission.html#check-before-you-submit)).
For example
`itsx_chimeric`, `itsx_no_5.8S`, or `itsx_boundary_shift(...)`. A grey "not run" means ITSx gave
no answer for the contig, and a grey "not checked" means no ITSx check is stored yet; the Checks
column lists both as "ITSx not checked". The **Chimera** column reports the
chimera check's level, see [Chimeras](#chimeras-contigs-made-of-two-pieces).
The **Feature BLAST warnings** column lists features whose own BLAST search
looks wrong, see [Feature BLAST](#feature-blast-each-feature-searched-on-its-own).

The contamination checks need a BLAST screen result. When a contig has none, for
example because NCBI could not be reached, RiboPilot does not skip the check: it
raises `contaminant_unchecked`, and triage flags the contig "BLAST screen has not
run".

`low_identity` needs the references sequences downloaded from NCBI. When they could
not be downloaded, the identity check is skipped with no warning, so a gene without
`low_identity` has not always been checked.

# The Checks column

The Checks column puts every check on one line, worst first, in a color that
matches the worst finding. On the Assemble table it summarizes all of the sample's kept
contigs.

| Checks says | Color | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| off target, contaminant, severe chimera, ITSx chimeric | red | Lock and the Export window ask first, until the contig is marked Reviewed. |
| minor chimera, uncertain screen, ITSx, ITSx not checked, warnings, feature flags | amber | Worth a look, but nothing asks when you Lock or Export. |
| ok | green | The best BLAST matches are in your sample's phylum, and nothing is flagged. |
| no reference | grey | Nothing is flagged, but the BLAST screen had no usable match to judge by. |

On Annotation Review, a contig whose checks are not finished shows its state in the
Checks column and in every check column (Warnings, ITSx Warnings, Screen, Chimera,
and the BLAST columns) instead, for example "not run" after a trim, until
**Update** on Annotation Review reruns its checks.

# What the BLAST screen searches

Contig BLAST search results are used in the Screen column, the contamination warnings above, the
triage rules below, and the chimera check.

By default each contig is searched against the **bundled rDNA database** inside the
container: about 600,000 animal nuclear rDNA records from GenBank, plus NCBI's
16S, eukaryote small subunit, and eukaryote large subunit rRNA sets. This means that a
contaminant bacterial, fungal, or plant contig still finds a match. Contigs that
match nothing in the bundled database are searched against the NCBI nucleotide database (core_nt),
over the internet.

To change how the BLAST search works, open a sample's **BLAST Options** in the Assemble module and pick a
**Search** choice: "Bundled database only" never goes to NCBI, and "NCBI only
(core_nt)" skips the bundled database. 

In Annotation Review, the **Hit Source** column says which
database was used to determine the assembly's best BLAST hit: "bundled", "NCBI", or "seed file"
(the assembly's own seed database, which is only a hint).

# Feature BLAST: each feature searched on its own

The contig BLAST search can look fine while one feature is wrong. A contig
search keeps its top 50 matches, and these mostly come from the long 18S and 28S
genes, so an ITS1 that matches nothing goes unnoticed. That can point to a poor
assembly or to contamination.

So RiboPilot also searches each core feature (18S, ITS1, 5.8S, ITS2, 28S) on
its own against the bundled rDNA database. It never goes to NCBI. This runs
after annotation, and again when **Update** rechecks a contig.

The **Feature BLAST warnings** column in Annotation Review lists only the
features that need a look:

| Warning | Meaning |
|---|---|
| no hit | Nothing in the database matched the feature. |
| non-rDNA hit | The best match is not a nuclear rDNA record. |
| off-target (Ascomycota) | The best match shares nothing with your sample at phylum level or below; the group in brackets is the match's phylum. |
| no BLAST, feature too small | The feature is under 50 bp, too short for a useful search. |

Very short pieces of DNA match many organisms equally well, so their matches say
little about who they came from. Features of 50 to 99 bp are searched but marked
low confidence. 5.8S is so conserved that it often matches many groups equally.

When several matches score almost the same, RiboPilot names the group they all
belong to instead of picking one, for example "Chordata (12 tied hits)". The
feature counts as off target only when that group, and every tied match, falls
outside your sample's phylum.

The **Feature BLAST** panel in a contig's details window shows every feature's
best match, how closely it matches your sample (species, genus, family, and so
on), and its percent identity and coverage. Expand a row to see the top 10
matches. If the database is not available, for example when an Update only
moves the original hits onto a trimmed contig, the features show "Not run".

The feature BLAST only reports. It does not change the Checks column, the
quality flags, triage, or export.

# How contigs are kept or dropped (auto-triage)

Warnings never modify your underlying assemblies or annotations. Instead, once a contig has been 
screened, RiboPilot proposes to keep or drop the contig by checking the eight rules below in order. 
For rules that are "flag only", the contig status stays undecided, and the **Why** column in
sample's contig table gives the reason. You can override any call by hand
with the **K** and **D** buttons in the Assemble details window.

| # | Rule | What it means | Can it drop? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Annotation has not run | Neither annotation tool has reported on this contig yet. | No, flag only |
| 2 | BLAST screen has not run | No usable BLAST hit is recorded, or the only matches are whole-genome assemblies, so the contig cannot be judged. | No, flag only |
| 3 | No annotations, non-rDNA hit | Annotation found no rRNA or ITS feature, and the best GenBank match is not a nuclear rDNA record. | Yes, dropped by default |
| 4 | No annotations but rDNA hit | Annotation found no rRNA or ITS feature, but the best GenBank match is a nuclear rDNA record. | Optional; flagged by default |
| 5 | Has annotations but non-rDNA hit | The annotation has a rRNA or ITS feature, but the best GenBank match is not a nuclear rDNA record. | Optional; flagged by default |
| 6 | GenBank taxonomy disagrees with the sample | The contig's BLAST hits agree on a taxon that is not close to your sample's lineage. | Optional; flagged by default |
| 7 | Disagrees with sibling contigs | This contig's top hit disagrees with the majority of this sample's other contigs. A hint, not proof. | No, flag only |
| 8 | Chimeric assembly (severe) | Parts of this contig match organisms from different phyla or kingdoms. | No, flag only |

The taxonomy rule compares the contig's BLAST hits with your sample's lineage
at phylum rank. It catches a fungal, bacterial, or plant contaminant, but
cannot separate two organisms in the same phylum.

To change what a rule does, select samples in the Assemble table and click on the
**Triage** button at the top. The Triage window allows you to set each rule to Off, Flag, or Drop, 
shows how many contigs each rule would decide, and
reruns the triage assessment for the selected samples when you click **Apply**.

# Chimeric contigs

A chimera is one assembled contig containing sequences that do not belong together.
For example, rDNA from two organisms or two different copies of the repeat from one genome.

RiboPilot checks for a chimeric contigs in four ways:

- **Gene by gene.** The 18S, 5.8S, and 28S genes each get their own best
  GenBank matches. Ideally these should agree on one lineage.
- **Along the contig.** Overlapping 200 bp windows, one every 100 bp, are
  searched against the bundled rDNA database. Neighboring windows that match the
  same class are joined into segments. Neighboring segments that hit different 
  taxonomic classes suggest a chimeric join. A switch between classes counts only
  when each side spans at least four windows (about 500 bp), because short
  conserved stretches often match another class of the same phylum. A switch
  between phyla or kingdoms needs only two windows on each side.
- **Gene structure.** The ribotyper tool checks that the 18S and 28S each look
  like one whole gene. ITSx's own chimera call adds a little weight.
- **Reads.** Many mapped reads that stop at exactly same point or major shift in read
  depth can indicate a chimeric assembly.

Each contig gets a chimera check levels, shown in the **Chimera** column of the
Annotation Review table and in the **Checks** column:

| Level | What it means | Triage | Export |
|---|---|---|---|
| severe | Two parts of the contig match different phyla or kingdoms, each at 90 percent identity or more. | The chimera rule flags the contig. | The `submission_risk` column says `chimeric(...)`, and Lock and the Export window ask first until the contig is marked Reviewed. |
| minor | Weaker evidence: contig BLAST search matches multiple classes, genes agree only at a high taxonomic rank, a ribotyper warning, or read evidence alone. | No rule fires. | Listed in the `chimera_warning` column of the summary CSV. It is not a submission risk, and neither Lock nor the Export window asks. |
| clean | Nothing found. | No rule fires. | Nothing. |

In the test project, CHIM01 is severe: the contig is an artificial chimera
composed of sequence from ray-finned fish and *Penicillium* mold.

![A real chimera in the sequence viewer: the origin track switches lineage at the junction](figures/get-started/assemble-chimera-chim01.png)

RiboPilot attempts to handle false alarms. Windows in conserved
stretches of 18S or 28S, where many groups match equally well, are shown as
"unresolved" and do not count. Depth changes inside sequence that repeats
elsewhere on the contig, or right at a gene boundary, are ignored, and so are
reads that stop near the ends of the contig. 

A weak signal can still give a
"minor" call. Below, the first contig of SRR33849683 is marked "minor" because its
genes agree only at phylum level, though every window that can be placed
matches a ray-finned fish:

![Chimera check for a weaker signal that needs a look](figures/curation/chimera-mild.png)

To judge a flag, open **Coverage and windowed BLAST** with **BLAST origin** ticked:
each stretch is coloured by the class its BLAST windows match (grey is your
lineage, white is no hit), **BLAST identity** shows the hit identity, and a
dashed line marks a possible junction; hover for the match. The **Chimera
check** panel below gives the call, the reason, and the segments; click a
segment, window, or junction row to zoom the viewer to it. A real chimera shows
a clean switch from one lineage to another at one point, often accompanied by a
shift in read depth. 

A lineage switch that sits inside a conserved stretch of
18S or 28S, to a group that is not far from yours, is usually a false alarm. If
in doubt, copy the contig with **Copy FASTA** and run your own BLAST searches on the 
NCBI website.

# Several contigs from one organism

When a sample assembles more than one rDNA contig, RiboPilot compares their
18S, 5.8S, and 28S genes. Results are show in in the **Variant** column of the 
Assemble step's contig table. Too little shared gene sequence gives "not comparable". 
A contaminant from the same phylum also passes the screen, so BLAST each
variant's ITS before you lock one.

An **isomer** is RiboPilot's label for contigs where the genes are (nearly) identical 
but they differ in the ITS sequence or flanking regions.

A **paralog** means the genes of the contigs differ. That can be real
variation within one genome (known in octocorals and jellyfish), contamination,
or a pseudogene. 

Handle isomers and paralogs with care. It may be best to consult the literature
for your group of organisms or examine a reference genome to see if rDNA paralogs/isomers
are a know phenomenon. 

# How the checks are tuned per group

The expected lengths and identity floors depend on the group of organisms.
RiboPilot ships five rulesets (parameterized by examining GenBank records):

| Ruleset | Used for samples in |
|---|---|
| `actinopterygii` | ray-finned fishes |
| `asteroidea` | sea stars |
| `scyphozoa` | true jellyfish |
| `octocorallia` | octocorals |
| `metazoa_generic` | any other group; the contig gets the `no_clade_ruleset` note |

To use another one, pick it as **Clade ruleset** in the sample's **Curate
Options** (Assemble step). Leaving `metazoa_generic` there lets RiboPilot choose
from the lineage.

Expected lengths, in bases. A `length` warning means a feature fell outside its
range, which is common and often fine for the spacers:

| Feature | Generic animal | Ray-finned fishes | Sea stars, jellyfish, octocorals |
|---|---|---|---|
| 18S | 1600 to 2100 | 1750 to 1950 | 1700 to 1900 |
| 5.8S | 140 to 180 | 140 to 175 | 150 to 170 |
| 28S | 2000 to 6000 | 2500 to 5000 | 2000 to 6000 |
| ITS1 | 120 to 1600 | 150 to 1200 | 120 to 1200 |
| ITS2 | 120 to 1600 | 150 to 1200 | 120 to 1200 |

Identity floors, in percent. Below these a gene gets `low_identity`:

| Gene | Generic animal | Ray-finned fishes | Sea stars, jellyfish, octocorals |
|---|---|---|---|
| 18S | 95 | 97 | 93 |
| 5.8S | 93 | 95 | 90 |
| 28S | 80 | 85 | 78 |

The floors are lower for sea stars, jellyfish, and octocorals because GenBank
has fewer rDNA records for these groups. All of these are working values, not
published standards: a `length` or `low_identity` warning is a prompt to look,
not a verdict. In every ruleset, a gene is `truncated` when
less than 90 percent of its rRNA model was recovered, and identity is judged only
when the reference covers at least half of the gene.

Want ranges for your own group? [Open an issue](https://github.com/dmacguigan/RiboPilot/issues)
describing it. Until then, the generic animal ruleset works for any group; it
is just more lenient.
